metadata.title: Gelfand Duality — Abstract Mathematical Exposition
metadata.subtitle: The abstract representation theorem
metadata.scope: The commutative unital Gelfand representation theorem for a nonzero complex C*-algebra.
metadata.purpose: Canonical mathematical content for the abstract Gelfand representation theorem, independent of any presentation or implementation.
metadata.reuseGuidance: Use these mathematical statements, definitions, explanations, equations, and theorem references as a self-contained source. The numbering records the logical progression of the proof, not a required display sequence. Presentation format, organization, and delivery are separate decisions.
metadata.notationNote: A denotes the original algebra; M a maximal ideal; X the character space; A* the continuous dual; a-hat the Gelfand transform of an element a; A-hat the image of the transform.

step.title: The objective
step.takeaway: Reconstruct a space from an algebra.
step.explanation: Starting with a commutative unital C*-algebra A, we will construct a compact Hausdorff space X and establish an isometric *-isomorphism between A and C(X).
step.detail: The proof constructs X from A and then establishes the isometric *-isomorphism.

step.title: Existence of maximal ideals
step.explanation: The proper ideals of A form a nonempty partially ordered set under inclusion. The union of any nonempty chain of proper ideals is itself a proper ideal and provides an upper bound.
step.detail: The union cannot contain the identity, since that would mean one of the proper ideals contains the identity.

step.title: Maximal ideals are closed
step.explanation: If the closure of a maximal ideal M contained the identity, M would contain an element sufficiently close to the identity to be invertible. This contradicts the properness of M.
step.detail: The closure is itself an ideal. Since it is proper and contains M, maximality forces equality.

step.title: Construct the quotient algebra
step.takeaway: Closedness gives a Banach quotient; maximality gives division.
step.explanation: Because M is closed, A/M is a unital complex Banach algebra. Because M is maximal, every nonzero coset is invertible.
step.detail: Consequently, there exist m in M and a in A such that m + ax = 1. Passing to the quotient establishes invertibility.

step.title: Obtain the characters
step.takeaway: Every complex Banach division algebra is isomorphic to ℂ.
step.explanation: The Gelfand–Mazur theorem applies to A/M. Composing the quotient map with the resulting isomorphism produces a character on A.
step.detail: The character φ = θ ∘ q is a nonzero multiplicative linear functional. Characters have norm one.

step.title: Construct the space X
step.explanation: Let X be the set of all characters. It is a weak-* closed subset of the closed unit ball of A*, and therefore compact by Banach–Alaoglu.
step.detail: Distinct characters differ on at least one element of A. The corresponding evaluation map separates them, establishing the Hausdorff property.

step.title: Define the Gelfand transform
step.takeaway: Elements of the algebra become functions on the character space.
step.explanation: For each element a of A, define a function on X by evaluating each character at a. Continuity follows from the definition of the weak-* topology.
step.detail: The character identities establish linearity and multiplicativity. Characters also preserve the involution, so the transform is a *-homomorphism.

step.title: Establish isometry
step.takeaway: The spectral radius recovers the original norm.
step.explanation: The character values of a constitute its spectrum. Since A is a commutative C*-algebra, every element is normal, and its spectral radius equals its norm.
step.detail: Isometry immediately establishes injectivity: two elements with the same transform must have distance zero.

step.title: Establish surjectivity
step.explanation: The image of A contains the constants, separates the points of X and is closed under complex conjugation. Stone–Weierstrass therefore establishes density in C(X).
step.detail: Isometry and completeness of A establish that the image is closed. Together with density, this proves surjectivity and completes the isometric *-isomorphism.

editorialNotes.note: For the empty chain, the zero ideal is an upper bound. The nonzero assumption ensures it is proper.
The weak-* closedness is relative to the closed unit ball: impose φ(1)=1 and the multiplicative identities for all pairs of algebra elements.
The identification of the spectrum with character values is an additional standard result from commutative unital Banach algebra theory.
The image is both dense and closed in the supremum norm. The displayed equality uses both arguments, not Stone–Weierstrass alone.
